Welcome to Western House Academy
Welcome
We are a three-form entry school nestled within the heart of Cippenham, on the Western edge of Slough. We are one of ten schools that form The Park Federation Academy Trust. Our community is culturally diverse and rich in aspiration giving our school a family-centred quality which we hugely value. Our children are encouraged to celebrate difference and diversity and to develop into caring, respectful young citizens who actively participate in all areas of life; our core values are evident in all we do.
We are proud to be part of The Park Federation Academy Trust.

Testimonials
Good evening Mrs Snowden I’d like to take a minute to thank your incredible nursery staff that have made xxxx and xxxx so comfortable that by Day 4 they were both skipping into nursery without a second look. This is something we didn’t achieve after six months at their last nursery, hence our decision to move them to Western House. To know my children feel happy and safe after such a short time is a relief and moving them to Western House was the best decision we have made for them. We are so overwhelmingly happy with how they have settled in, made friends and picked up the routine Your team is an absolute credit to the school - a small thing such as making the effort to learn who is who rather than referring to them as “the twins”, looking for distinguishing features and personality traits has made such an impact on us as parents, and on the girls coming home excitingly telling us they’ve been called the right name! No more tears from xxxxx, xxxxx or Mummy!
I just wanted to express my gratitude for the invitation to attend the Values Award ceremony today. My daughter xxxxxx in year 6 has only just begun her journey at your school in September 2024. To say she is thriving in her new environment is an understatement - today was testimony of that! It was very emotional and touching to see her being valued and rewarded for the wonderful traits that she possess and the fact that the fellow pupils and staff at WHA see this in her too. It was also such a delight to see a head teacher who genuinely looked so full of pride and joy for each and every one of her pupils. From working in childcare myself, I know it takes a true love of your job to be able to give all your support and nurturing to you children you care for and Mrs Snowden radiates this. We look forward to many more achievements and goals of accomplishment for xxxxx as she spends her final year with WHA. Thank you to everyone for all the hard work and effort that goes in to each and every day.
I wanted to say a HUGE thank you for two events: camping on the school grounds in year 5 and residential trip to Woodrow House in year 6. My daughter absolutely loved both trips. The teachers and the staff were just incredible, I can't thank them enough. I was rather worried about the camping, because it was cold and rainy. But the teachers organised fantastic games in the hall, the children went outside when the rain stopped. They had a talent show in the evening, which was a highlight of the day. The bbq and hot chocolate in the evening were lovely. They were obviously too excited to sleep at night, but they felt secure. The teachers were around all the time. In the morning both the head teacher and vice principal came early to serve the children breakfast. Apparently the best toasts my daughter has ever had! Then they went to the classroom for lessons. The children were allowed to finish that day earlier. My daughter wasn't cold or wet or hungry or scared. She enjoyed the whole experience so much. The residential trip to Woodrow House was another wonderful and well organised event. The activities were fun, interesting and challenging. They had a campfire with funny games and lots of giggles. The food was amazing and there was a good selection. My daughter loved being able to share the bedroom with all her friends. And the tuck shop was an absolute hit! One of the teachers was offering hugs before bedtime, which I also think was extremely kind! I am very grateful for the commitment and dedication of everyone involved in ensuring that these events were so successful.
We just wanted to say a heartfelt and warm thank you from the bottom of our hearts for taking care of our children and giving them the best ever memories that will last a life time. They have been truly spoilt and are such lucky boys to have been given this opportunity and we as parents cannot thank you enough for making this happen. They have come back this evening so excited and exhausted all rolled in to one and sharing all the wonderful things they have done. We also wanted to thank you for the constant updates whilst out there and pictures we received. It felt like we were with them on the trip and definitely put our minds at ease. Hopefully you will catch up on some sleep and have a well deserved rest. Our sincere thanks again for giving the boys an experience they’ll never forget.
I am sure you will be getting lots of messages but I just wanted to say a massive thank you for the wonderful trip that XXXX has come back from, he was telling us lots about his adventures and what his favourite part was on the way home last night. At 7.30am he is still asleep which never happens. He was a little anxious about going to start with and the closer it got he got a bit more worried, but he had such a great time. The updates via the Whatsapp group and photos were very much appreciated especially seeing all the smiling faces. Please pass my thanks onto all the adults that attended and I do hope that you all managed to enjoy yourselves as well. Roll on the weekend for a much deserved drink and rest. I hope this is the start to lots more trips to Paris for you. I have to admit my older two kids, if you can call them that now, were very jealous when they heard their little brother was off to Paris as they went to Dorset in Year 5 :-)

PE and Sport Premium
PE and Sports Funding
The Primary PE and Sport Premium is a government-backed funding initiative aimed at helping primary schools across England improve their physical education and sport provisions. The premium is designed to help children get an active start in life, supporting primary schools to improve the quality of their PE, physical activity/literacy, and sport provision so that pupils experience the benefits of regular exercise.
Our Aims

As a result, our aim is to ensure that we use the money afforded to us through the sports premium effectively in developing a rich, broad and high quality PE and extra-curricular provision to all of our pupils, which enables our children to improve their health, fitness, mental well-being and academic achievement whilst developing a life-long love for physical activity.

The Implementation of the Curriculum at WHA
Every subject in the curriculum offered at WHA stands on four broad principles; values, knowledge, equality and experience. These underpin every decision teachers make in order to teach effectively. We promote our values in every aspect of the curriculum and encourage collaborative work as well as individual scholarships. The knowledge taught is based upon the National Curriculum and the knowledge experiences and skills lower down the school feed into the subjects and units in the upper school, ensuring progress and a wealth of knowledge for the children to draw upon as they meet new challenges and learning. Children have meaningful experiences in their learning, the breadth of the curriculum is designed, so no subject is left out and every subject has integrity.
We have carefully constructed a curriculum that enables us to focus on one humanities subject each half term, giving it the integrity it needs. Leavers Legacy
At Western House Academy, we want our pupils to know that they can make a difference — not only while they are with us, but long after they have moved on.
Our Leave a Legacy initiative gives our Year 6 pupils the opportunity to create something meaningful that will benefit future generations of children at WHA and, in some cases, our wider community.
Each year, our Head Pupils lead their year group on a special project, gathering ideas, listening to their peers and working together to decide how they would like to leave their mark. From developing the initial idea through to bringing their vision to life, pupils take ownership of creating a legacy that will continue long after they leave WHA.
Leave a Legacy is about much more than leaving something physical behind. It provides our oldest pupils with a genuine opportunity to demonstrate leadership, teamwork, ambition, courage and social responsibility. Most importantly, it shows our children that their ideas matter and that they have the power to make a positive difference.
Our Leave a Legacy Projects
📚 Reading Swap Boxes
Our pupils introduced Reading Swap Boxes on the playground, giving children the opportunity to bring, swap and share books. Their legacy continues to promote a love of reading while making books easily accessible for children to enjoy and share with one another.
🏆 Developing Our House System
Our pupils helped to develop the WHA House System, creating something that has become an important part of school life. The House System provides opportunities for children across different year groups to work together, celebrate achievements and develop an even stronger sense of belonging to the WHA community.
🤝 Learning and Teaching Makaton
One year group chose to make WHA an even more inclusive place by learning Makaton and teaching it to children across the school. Their project helped pupils understand that there are many different ways to communicate and reinforced the importance of inclusion and ensuring that everyone's voice can be heard.
🌱 Community Allotment Project
Our Year 6 pupils took their Leave a Legacy initiative beyond the school gates through a community project to develop an allotment. The project created an opportunity for pupils to think about how they could make a positive and lasting contribution to the wider community.
Through their involvement, pupils explored sustainability, growing food and caring for the environment, while recognising the importance of contributing to and caring for the community around them.
🌿 Developing an Outdoor Learning Space
Our most recent Year 6 cohort chose to leave their mark on WHA by helping to develop an open outdoor space for learning.
Their vision was to create an inspiring and flexible area where children could take their learning beyond the classroom, providing opportunities to learn, explore, collaborate and enjoy being outdoors.
This project will provide a lasting learning environment that can be enjoyed by children across WHA for many years to come. It is a wonderful example of our Year 6 pupils thinking beyond their own time at the school and creating something that will benefit the pupils who follow in their footsteps.
Every Leave a Legacy project is different because every Year 6 cohort brings its own ideas, passions and personality. Some leave behind a physical space, others introduce a new skill or opportunity, and some create something that becomes embedded in everyday school life.
Together, these projects are becoming part of the history and story of Western House Academy.
Leave a Legacy brings our school motto, “Where every opportunity shapes a life,” to life. By giving our pupils the opportunity to lead meaningful change, we hope they leave WHA knowing that they have a voice, their actions matter and they have the power to make a positive difference wherever they go.
Their time at WHA may come to an end, but their legacy lives on.
